modernSlavery.title: Modern Slavery Statement
modernSlavery.description: Our modern slavery statement outlines the steps Harch Corp takes to prevent slavery, forced labor, and human trafficking in our operations and supply chains.
modernSlavery.ceoStatement1: “At Harch Corp, we believe that the dignity of every human being is non-negotiable. Modern slavery, in all its forms — forced labor, human trafficking, debt bondage, and child labor — represents a fundamental violation of human rights that has no place in our operations or supply chain. As a Moroccan industrial conglomerate operating across seven verticals and multiple geographies, we recognize both our responsibility and our influence to drive positive change.
modernSlavery.ceoStatement2: Our commitment goes beyond compliance. We actively seek to identify and eradicate modern slavery risks throughout our value chain, from the mines that supply our raw materials to the technology partners who power our digital infrastructure. We invest in due diligence, training, and remediation because we understand that building Africa's industrial sovereignty must be built on a foundation of respect for human rights.
modernSlavery.ceoStatement3: This statement sets out the steps we have taken during the fiscal year 2025 to prevent modern slavery and human trafficking in our business and supply chains, and it reflects our unwavering commitment to continuous improvement.”
modernSlavery.ceoTitle: Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Harch Corp
modernSlavery.businessDescription: Harch Corp is a Moroccan multi-sector industrial conglomerate headquartered in Casablanca, Morocco. We operate across seven core verticals: AI data centers and intelligence infrastructure (1,798 GPU capacity), renewable energy generation and distribution (2GW+ Renewable Pipeline), cement and construction materials manufacturing, sovereign technology and cybersecurity services, strategic mining operations including phosphates and critical minerals, precision agriculture and vertical farming, and water infrastructure including desalination and treatment. Our supply chain spans multiple countries across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, and includes raw material suppliers, equipment manufacturers, construction contractors, technology providers, logistics companies, and professional service firms. The diversity and scale of our operations present inherent modern slavery risks, particularly in labor-intensive sectors such as construction, mining, and agriculture, and in regions where regulatory frameworks may be less robust.
modernSlavery.policiesIntro: We have established a comprehensive framework of policies and due diligence processes to identify, prevent, and mitigate modern slavery risks:
modernSlavery.supplierCodeDescription: All suppliers and contractors are required to acknowledge and comply with our Supplier Code of Conduct, which explicitly prohibits forced labor, child labor, human trafficking, and all forms of modern slavery. The code requires suppliers to provide fair wages, safe working conditions, and freedom of movement for all workers.
modernSlavery.supplierDueDiligenceDescription: All new suppliers undergo a risk-based due diligence assessment before onboarding, which includes screening for modern slavery indicators, review of labor practices and working conditions, verification of recruitment agencies and labor intermediaries, assessment of geographic and sector-specific risks, and evaluation of the supplier's own policies and monitoring mechanisms. High-risk suppliers are subject to enhanced due diligence, including on-site audits conducted by independent third-party auditors.
modernSlavery.internalControlsDescription: Our internal controls include rigorous recruitment and employment practices that verify the identity and legal right to work of all employees, prohibition of recruitment fees charged to workers, direct payment of wages to employees through transparent payroll systems, regular monitoring of working hours and conditions, and accessible grievance mechanisms for all workers, including subcontracted labor.
modernSlavery.riskAssessmentIntro: We conduct annual risk assessments to identify and evaluate modern slavery risks across our operations and supply chain. Our risk assessment methodology considers:

riskAssessmentItems.label: Sector-specific risks:
riskAssessmentItems.description: Mining, construction, and agriculture are identified as higher-risk sectors due to the prevalence of migrant labor, informal employment practices, and hazardous working conditions.

riskAssessmentItems.label: Geographic risks:
riskAssessmentItems.description: Operations and supply chains in regions with weaker labor protections, high levels of migration, or conflict-affected areas receive heightened scrutiny.

riskAssessmentItems.label: Labor provider risks:
riskAssessmentItems.description: The use of third-party labor providers, recruitment agencies, and subcontractors introduces additional risks that are managed through enhanced due diligence and contractual safeguards.

riskAssessmentItems.label: Raw material risks:
riskAssessmentItems.description: The sourcing of critical minerals and raw materials, particularly from artisanal and small-scale mining operations, carries inherent risks that require specialized monitoring and traceability measures.

modernSlavery.keyActionsIntro: During fiscal year 2025, we took the following actions to combat modern slavery in our operations and supply chain:
keyActions: Conducted 47 on-site supplier audits across all seven verticals, with 12 audits specifically focused on high-risk suppliers in the construction and mining sectors. Identified 3 non-conformities related to working hours documentation and took immediate corrective action.
Implemented a digital supply chain traceability platform for our mining and agriculture verticals, enabling end-to-end visibility of labor practices from raw material extraction to final delivery.

Terminated relationships with 2 suppliers who failed to demonstrate adequate controls against modern slavery after a remediation period. These terminations were conducted in accordance with our responsible exit protocol to minimize adverse impacts on workers.
Established a dedicated Human Rights and Supply Chain Integrity team within the Compliance Office, staffed with specialists in labor rights, supply chain management, and social auditing.
Adopted the Employer Pays Principle across all our operations, ensuring that no worker bears the cost of recruitment to obtain employment with Harch Corp or its suppliers.
modernSlavery.trainingDescription: During fiscal year 2025, we delivered modern slavery awareness training to 100% of our employees and key contractor personnel. Training programs included mandatory e-learning modules for all employees on identifying and reporting modern slavery, specialized in-person workshops for procurement and supply chain teams, targeted training for site managers and supervisors on labor rights and worker welfare, training for HR professionals on ethical recruitment practices and the Employer Pays Principle, and awareness sessions for senior leadership on emerging regulatory requirements and best practices. In total, over 2,800 hours of training were delivered, and we achieved a 96% completion rate across all mandatory modules.
modernSlavery.effectivenessIntro: We measure the effectiveness of our actions to combat modern slavery through the following key performance indicators:

kpiTable.indicator: Grievances related to labor practices received

modernSlavery.nextStepsIntro: Looking ahead to fiscal year 2026, we plan to:
nextSteps: Expand our digital supply chain traceability platform to cover 100% of our tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers across all verticals.
Implement worker voice technology in our mining and agriculture operations to enable direct and anonymous feedback from workers.
Commission an independent third-party assessment of our modern slavery due diligence framework and implement its recommendations.
Enhance collaboration with industry peers, civil society organizations, and government agencies to share best practices and drive systemic change.
Conduct a comprehensive review of our recruitment agency framework across all operations, with particular focus on cross-border labor migration pathways.
modernSlavery.approvalDescription: This Modern Slavery Statement has been approved by the Board of Directors of Harch Corp and is published in accordance with the UK Modern Slavery Act 2015, Section 54, the Australian Modern Slavery Act 2018 (Cth), and our voluntary commitment to transparency under the Kingdom of Morocco's legal framework.
modernSlavery.footerNote: Published: January 2026 | This statement is governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Morocco.

sla.title: Service Level Agreement
sla.description: Our Service Level Agreement defines the availability commitments, performance targets, and remediation processes that govern Harch Corp infrastructure and platform services.
sla.serviceAvailabilityDescription: Harch Corp is committed to providing highly available and reliable services to our clients. Our Service Level Agreement guarantees a monthly uptime target of 99.95% for all covered services, including our digital platform, API endpoints, and managed infrastructure. This commitment reflects our investment in enterprise-grade infrastructure, redundant systems, and 24/7 operations monitoring across our data centers and service delivery platforms.
sla.measurementMethodologyIntro: Service availability is measured on a monthly basis using the following methodology:
sla.measurementUptime: Uptime Percentage is calculated as: (Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) ÷ Total Minutes in Month × 100
sla.measurementDowntime: Downtime is defined as the period during which the covered service is unavailable and responds with errors or does not respond to valid requests for more than 5 consecutive minutes.
sla.measurementMonitoring: Monitoring is performed by independent third-party monitoring services from at least three geographically distributed locations. A service is considered down only when confirmed by at least two monitoring locations simultaneously.
sla.measurementPeriod: Measurement Period runs from 00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month to 23:59 UTC on the last day of the month.
sla.scheduledMaintenanceDescription: To ensure the continued reliability and security of our services, we perform scheduled maintenance windows. Maintenance windows are typically scheduled on the first Saturday of each month between 02:00 UTC and 06:00 UTC. We provide at least 72 hours advance notice for planned maintenance through our status page and email notifications to registered contacts. Emergency maintenance may be performed without advance notice when necessary to address critical security vulnerabilities or service-threatening conditions. Scheduled maintenance downtime is excluded from availability calculations.
sla.serviceCreditsIntro: If we fail to meet the service availability target in a given month, affected clients are entitled to service credits as follows:
sla.serviceCreditsNote: Service credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the SLA target. Credits are applied automatically to the next billing cycle and are not refundable in cash. The maximum aggregate credit for a single month shall not exceed 75% of the monthly service fee. To receive credits, clients must continue to be current on their payment obligations.
sla.exclusionsIntro: The SLA does not apply to downtime or performance issues resulting from the following:
exclusions: Scheduled maintenance windows as communicated in advance
Issues caused by factors outside our reasonable control (force majeure events, natural disasters, government actions)
Downtime resulting from client misconfiguration, unauthorized modifications, or misuse of the services
Failures of client-provided equipment, software, or network connectivity
Issues arising from third-party services or integrations not managed by Harch Corp
Temporary interruptions during emergency security patching or critical vulnerability remediation
Degradation of service performance due to client exceeding allocated resource quotas
sla.claimsProcessIntro: To submit an SLA claim, clients must follow the process outlined below:
sla.claimsStep1Description: Submit a claim to support@harchcorp.com within 30 calendar days of the end of the month in which the downtime occurred. Claims must include the affected service, dates and times of downtime, and any supporting evidence or logs.
sla.claimsStep2Description: Our team will review the claim against our monitoring data and system logs within 15 business days. We may request additional information from the client during this review period.
sla.claimsStep3Description: If the claim is validated, the applicable service credit will be applied to the client's next invoice. We will provide written confirmation of the credit amount and the billing period to which it applies.
sla.contactIntro: For SLA-related inquiries, claims, or support requests, please contact our support team:
sla.contactAddress: Address: Harch Corp, 123 Boulevard Mohammed V, Casablanca 20000, Morocco
sla.footerNote: Last updated: January 2026 | This SLA is governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Morocco.

trademark.usageDescription: Proper use of Harch Corp trademarks is essential to maintaining their legal protection and the strength of our brand. Please follow these guidelines when referring to Harch Corp trademarks:
trademark.usageSymbolDescription: Use the ® symbol for registered trademarks and the ™ symbol for trademarks pending registration or unregistered marks. The symbol should appear in superscript immediately after the trademark, on its first and most prominent use in any document or webpage. Example: HarchOS® or Harch Shield™.
trademark.usageAdjectiveDescription: Always use Harch Corp trademarks as adjectives, never as nouns or verbs. They should be followed by the generic term for the product or service. Correct: “the HarchOS platform”; Incorrect: “powered by HarchOS” without a following generic term. This preserves the distinctiveness of the mark.
trademark.usageDistinguishDescription: Make Harch Corp trademarks visually distinct from surrounding text through capitalization, bold or italic formatting, or quotation marks. Never use all lowercase for our trademarks. Example: “Harch Energy” or Harch Energy, never “harch energy.”
trademark.usageOwnershipDescription: Include a trademark attribution notice in all materials that use Harch Corp trademarks. The attribution should appear in a footnote or at the end of the document. Example: “Harch, HarchOS, and Harch Intelligence are registered trademarks of Harch Corp All rights reserved.”
trademark.usageAbbreviateDescription: Do not abbreviate, shorten, or create acronyms from Harch Corp trademarks. Always use the full, proper form of the trademark. Example: use “Harch Intelligence,” not “HI” or “Harch Intel.”
trademark.logoDescription: The Harch Corp logo is a critical element of our brand identity. When authorized to use our logo, you must adhere to the following rules:
trademark.logoClearSpaceDescription: The logo must have a minimum clear space equal to the height of the “H” in “Harch” on all sides. No other graphic elements, text, or visual elements may encroach on this clear space area.
trademark.logoMinimumSizeDescription: The logo must not be reproduced smaller than 24 pixels in height for digital applications or 8mm in height for print applications. This ensures legibility and preserves the integrity of the mark.
trademark.logoApprovedVersionsDescription: Use only approved versions of the Harch Corp logo as provided by our brand team. Do not recreate, redraw, or modify the logo. Approved versions include the full-color version (white on dark backgrounds), the monochrome version, and the icon-only version for specific applications.
trademark.logoBackgroundDescription: The logo must only be placed on backgrounds that provide sufficient contrast. The white version is for dark backgrounds, and the dark version is for light backgrounds. Do not place the logo over busy images, patterns, or backgrounds that compromise readability.
trademark.colorDescription: The Harch Corp brand uses a carefully defined color palette and typography system. When producing materials that reference our brand:
trademark.colorPrimaryDescription: White (#FFFFFF) is the primary brand color, used for the logo and key typographic elements. Dark background (#1A1A1A) serves as the foundation of our visual identity, reflecting our industrial precision and technological sophistication.
trademark.colorTypographyDescription: Inter is our primary typeface for body text and user interfaces. Space Mono is our secondary typeface used for data, labels, and technical notation. Do not substitute these typefaces with alternatives without written approval.
trademark.colorAccentDescription: Our accent colors include muted gray tones (#999999 for secondary text, #666666 for tertiary elements). These are used sparingly and must not dominate or compete with the primary palette.
trademark.colorProhibitedDescription: Do not apply unauthorized colors to the Harch Corp logo or brand materials. The logo must only appear in its approved color versions (white on dark, dark on light). Gradient or multi-color treatments are strictly prohibited.
trademark.notAllowedDescription: The following uses of Harch Corp trademarks are strictly prohibited without prior written authorization:
notAllowedItems: Using Harch Corp trademarks in a way that implies endorsement, partnership, or sponsorship without written authorization from Harch Corp
Modifying, distorting, or altering the Harch Corp logo or any trademark in any way, including changing colors, proportions, or adding effects.
Using Harch Corp trademarks as part of your own company name, product name, domain name, or social media handle.
Displaying the Harch Corp logo alongside competitor trademarks or in contexts that could create confusion about the source of products or services.
Using Harch Corp trademarks on merchandise, promotional items, or commercial products without explicit written permission.
Incorporating Harch Corp trademarks into your own logos, icons, or brand identifiers.
Using Harch Corp trademarks in any manner that is misleading, defamatory, obscene, or otherwise objectionable.
Registering or attempting to register any Harch Corp trademark or confusingly similar marks as domain names, social media handles, or trade names.
Using Harch Corp trademarks in metadata, hidden text, or keyword advertising (including Google Ads) to divert traffic from Harch Corp's own digital properties.
Creating derivative works based on Harch Corp trademarks, including parodies that could dilute the brand or tarnish its reputation.
trademark.requestDescription: If you wish to use any Harch Corp trademark or logo in a manner not expressly covered by these guidelines, you must obtain prior written permission from our brand team. Permission requests should include:
requestItems: The specific trademark(s) you wish to use
A detailed description of the intended use, context, and distribution
Visual mockups or samples of how the trademark will appear
The intended duration and geographic scope of use
trademark.requestAddress: Harch Corp, 123 Boulevard Mohammed V, Casablanca 20000, Morocco
trademark.requestResponseTime: We aim to respond to all permission requests within 10 business days.
trademark.footerNote: Last updated: January 2026 | All trademarks are the property of Harch Corp and are protected under the laws of the Kingdom of Morocco and international trademark conventions.

items.q: What is the Harch Corp platform?
items.a: Harch Corp is a Moroccan-domiciled industrial conglomerate with eight wholly-owned subsidiaries spanning cement, energy, intelligence, mining, agriculture, water, technology, and finance — orchestrated by in-house software (HarchOS + HarchLink).
Yes — each subsidiary is a standalone business with its own P&L, but all eight share one balance sheet, one procurement function, and one software stack inside Harch Corp.
Morocco (headquarters), Senegal, Kenya, Ghana, and Gambia — a sovereign industrial corridor spanning West and East Africa.
Harch Finance structures green bonds, sukuk, project finance, trade finance, and impact equity. Capital never leaves the group — it deploys across the eight verticals.
Yes. External capital participates via Harch Finance instruments — green bonds, sukuk, co-investment vehicles, and the sovereign facility. All instruments are Deloitte-audited and MIGA-covered.
HarchOS is the in-house workload orchestrator — it schedules GPU compute, energy dispatch, and cement production against grid carbon intensity and offtake demand.

privacy.description: We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the security of your personal data. This policy outlines how Harch Corp collects, uses, and safeguards your information in compliance with Moroccan Law No. 09-08, the GDPR, and international best practices.

cta.title: Questions About Your Data?
cta.description: Our Data Protection Officer is available to address any concerns about how we handle your information.

privacy.contactUsText: For any questions about this privacy policy or our data practices, contact us at dpo@harchcorp.com or write to Harch Corp, 123 Boulevard Mohammed V, Casablanca 20000, Morocco.
privacy.cookiesText: We use cookies to improve your experience, analyze site traffic, and deliver personalized content. You can manage your cookie preferences at any time.
privacy.dataCollectionText: We collect personal data that you provide directly, such as your name, email address, organization, and project details when you submit a quote request or contact us. We also automatically collect usage data, device information, and cookies when you visit our website.
privacy.dataSecurityText: We implement industry-standard security measures including AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. All data is processed on sovereign Moroccan infrastructure.
privacy.dataSharingText: We share your data only with trusted service providers who assist in delivering our services, and only under strict contractual obligations. We never sell your data. Cross-border transfers are protected by appropriate safeguards.
privacy.dataUseText: We use your personal data to process your requests, deliver our services, communicate with you about your projects, and improve our platform. We do not sell your personal data to third parties.
privacy.internationalTransfersText: When data transfers outside Morocco are necessary, we ensure adequate protection through Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy decisions, or other legally compliant mechanisms in accordance with Law 09-08 and GDPR.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.yourRightsText: You have the right to access, rectify, delete, and port your personal data. You may also object to processing or withdraw consent at any time. To exercise these rights, contact dpo@harchcorp.com.

intelligence.name: Harch Intelligence
intelligence.heroTitle:
Africa's Largest AI
Hyperscale Data Center
intelligence.heroSubtitle: 1,798 carbon-optimized GPUs across 5 hubs — sovereign AI compute infrastructure powered by Africa's lowest-carbon electricity
intelligence.overview: Harch Intelligence targets 1,798 carbon-optimized GPUs across 5 hubs in Morocco () — powered primarily by renewable energy and designed to serve as the backbone of Africa's sovereign AI compute infrastructure. With carbon-aware scheduling as our #1 differentiator, we route workloads to the greenest hubs in real time, targeting an average carbon intensity of 48.2 gCO2/kWh — 89% below the industry average. Our 500MW Pipeline in Dakhla positions Morocco as the gateway for AI compute between Europe and Africa, leveraging the country's exceptional renewable energy resources, strategic Atlantic coastline with submarine cable landing stations, and political stability. Direct connectivity to 3 submarine cable systems (Marea, ACE, AA-1) provides less than 8 ms latency to Europe, establishing Dakhla as the gateway of choice between Africa and global AI markets.  — pipeline.
intelligence.strategicContext: The global AI infrastructure race is accelerating, with over $300 billion invested in data center capacity in 2024 alone. Yet Africa, home to 1.4 billion people and the world's fastest-growing digital economy, hosts less than 1% of global data center capacity. This structural deficit forces African enterprises, governments, and researchers to rely on foreign infrastructure — creating dependencies that compromise data sovereignty, increase latency, and extract capital from the continent. Harch Intelligence directly addresses this imbalance by building sovereign AI compute capacity at the scale the continent demands. Our 5 hubs across Morocco deliver 1,798 GPUs with carbon-aware scheduling, and our 500MW Pipeline in Dakhla positions Morocco as the gateway for AI compute between Europe and Africa, leveraging the country's exceptional renewable energy resources, strategic Atlantic coastline with submarine cable landing stations, and political stability.
intelligence.marketAnalysis: Africa's cloud and data center market is projected to reach $15 billion by 2028, growing at 25% CAGR — the fastest growth rate globally. Key demand drivers include government data localization mandates sweeping across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Egypt; the explosive growth of African fintech processing over $500 billion annually; the expansion of AI-driven healthcare diagnostics serving 300 million patients; and the rise of sovereign AI initiatives from the African Union and regional bodies. Harch Intelligence's 1,798 GPUs across 5 hubs capture a significant share of this demand while operating at cost structures 40-60% cheaper than AWS/GCP/Azure, thanks to Dakhla's renewable energy costs of $0.03/kWh — among the lowest on the planet. Our carbon-aware scheduling achieves 48.2 gCO2/kWh average carbon intensity, 89% below the industry average of ~450 gCO2/kWh.
intelligence.sustainability: Every aspect of Harch Intelligence is designed for minimal environmental impact and maximum sustainability. The facility is targeted to run on 100% renewable energy from Harch Energy's solar and wind installations, eliminating scope 2 emissions entirely. Our hybrid liquid-air cooling system targets a PUE of 1.10 — among the most efficient in the global industry — while using seawater for heat rejection to minimize freshwater consumption. Waste heat from GPU clusters is captured and directed to adjacent agricultural greenhouses, creating a circular energy model. The facility's construction uses 40% recycled steel and low-carbon concrete from Harch Cement, while all electronic waste follows certified recycling protocols. We target LEED Platinum and BREEAM Outstanding certifications. .

capabilities.title: Carbon-Aware Data Centers
capabilities.desc: Five GPU hubs across Morocco engineered around carbon-aware scheduling as our primary differentiator. Our 500 MW Pipeline in Dakhla is purpose-built for the most demanding compute workloads — from foundation model training to real-time inference at scale — with modular architecture that scales from 100 MW to 500 MW in three phases. Every hub features dual redundant power paths, diverse fiber entrances from separate providers, and N+1 cooling redundancy across all thermal zones. Each rack is factory-pre-wired for direct liquid cooling, enabling next-generation GPU deployment — Blackwell, Rubin, and beyond — with zero retrofit cost or downtime. Our proprietary HarchOS scheduler continuously monitors grid carbon intensity across all five sites in real time, automatically routing workloads to the greenest available capacity without requiring any application-level changes from developers.

capabilities.title: GPU Clusters
capabilities.desc: 1,798 GPUs distributed across five hubs, each optimized for distinct workload profiles with carbon-aware scheduling at the orchestration layer. Harch Ouarzazate leads with 800 GPUs at 97.2% renewable energy and a carbon intensity of just 18 gCO2/kWh — enabling distributed training across full 800-GPU partitions for large-scale foundation models with industry-leading carbon efficiency. Harch Dakhla contributes 400 GPUs at 94.8% renewable (32 gCO2/kWh), purpose-built for sustained training runs. Harch Benguerir adds 350 GPUs at 88.5% renewable (55 gCO2/kWh), optimized for fine-tuning and batch inference. Harch Tanger provides 200 GPUs at 82.1% renewable (95 gCO2/kWh), positioned for low-latency inference serving European clients. Harch Casablanca operates 48 GPUs at 45% renewable (210 gCO2/kWh), serving as our urban inference edge for Morocco's domestic market. All clusters are interconnected via 400 Gbps fabric, enabling cross-hub distributed training with linear scaling efficiency above 92%.

capabilities.title: Renewable Energy Integration
capabilities.desc: 82.3% average renewable energy across all hubs, powered by Harch Energy's dedicated solar and wind infrastructure — not purchased offsets or renewable energy credits, but direct physical connection to generation assets we own and operate. Carbon-aware scheduling routes workloads to the greenest hub in real time, achieving a blended average of 48.2 gCO2/kWh — 89% below the industry average of ~450 gCO2/kWh. Zero-carbon electricity at Ouarzazate and Dakhla delivers cost advantages of 40-60% cheaper than AWS, GCP, and Azure equivalent regions, with energy costs as low as $0.018/kWh at Dakhla — 72% below the European average. On-site battery storage totaling 200 MWh provides backup for uninterrupted operations during grid transitions, while grid-scale power purchase agreements lock in pricing predictability for 15-year terms, insulating clients from volatile energy markets.

capabilities.title: Submarine Connectivity
capabilities.desc: Direct connection to three submarine cable systems — Marea, ACE (Africa Coast to Europe), and AA-1 (Africa-Asia-1) — providing ultra-low latency to Europe (8 ms to London and Paris), the Americas (35 ms to Virginia), and the Middle East (20 ms to Dubai). Dual diverse landing stations at separate physical locations ensure full path redundancy for all international traffic, eliminating single points of failure at the cable layer. Our Dakhla campus is planned to sit directly adjacent to the cable landing station, minimizing terrestrial backhaul to under 2 km. Combined with 3 major cable systems serving Moroccan waters and capacity exceeding 80 Tbps, this infrastructure positions Harch Intelligence as the lowest-latency bridge between African compute and European, American, and Middle Eastern markets — a connectivity advantage that cannot be replicated by inland European data centers. .

capabilities.title: Sovereign Security
capabilities.desc: End-to-end security from physical perimeter to data encryption, designed for clients who require sovereign-grade data protection. Facilities operate under a sovereign security framework with armed perimeter security, biometric access controls at every layer, and 24/7 surveillance with AI-powered anomaly detection. Harch Technology's cybersecurity suite provides sovereign-grade protection including real-time DDoS mitigation capable of absorbing multi-terabit attacks, deep packet inspection with intrusion detection and prevention, and encrypted data pathways using hardware security modules (HSMs) for sensitive compute workloads. Data residency is guaranteed within Moroccan borders under the Kingdom's data sovereignty regulations, with no data traversing foreign jurisdictions during processing. All access is logged immutably, and compliance artifacts are generated automatically for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR audit requirements.

capabilities.title: AI Platform Services
capabilities.desc: Full-stack AI platform spanning the entire lifecycle from data ingestion and preprocessing through model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and production deployment. Managed services for training, fine-tuning, and inference with enterprise SLAs guaranteeing 99.99% availability and sub-second model serving latency at the edge. The platform natively supports PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX with one-click cluster provisioning, and includes pre-built MLOps pipelines for automated model lifecycle management — from experiment tracking and hyperparameter optimization to canary deployments and automated rollback. Our model registry provides version control, lineage tracking, and governance controls for production models, while the inference engine supports dynamic batching, speculative decoding, and automatic model parallelism to maximize GPU utilization and minimize cost per token.

capabilities.title: Sustainable Compute Economics
capabilities.desc: Our compute pricing fundamentally undercuts hyperscaler economics by leveraging Morocco's structural energy advantages. Renewable electricity at $0.018/kWh in Dakhla — 72% below the European average — combined with free cooling for ~8,500 hours per year (average temperature 22°C) and zero property tax incentives, translates to GPU training costs 40-60% below equivalent AWS P5, GCP A3, or Azure ND H100 instances. Carbon-aware scheduling amplifies these savings further by shifting non-urgent workloads to the greenest, cheapest hubs during peak renewable generation hours. Enterprise clients benefit from transparent, predictable pricing with no egress fees for data transferred within the Harch network, and committed-use discounts that reward long-term capacity reservations with up to 35% additional savings over on-demand rates.

cement.name: Harch Cement
cement.heroSubtitle: 500kT/yr cement production serving the construction boom with vertically integrated operations
cement.overview: Harch Cement is developing a 500kT/yr cement production facility in Gambia, serving West Africa's construction boom with vertically integrated operations from quarry to delivery. Our model captures the full value chain — from limestone extraction through clinker production to finished cement distribution — creating structural cost advantages of 30-50% versus import-dependent competitors. This is not simply a cement plant; it is an industrial anchor that catalyzes infrastructure development, creates hundreds of direct jobs, and eliminates West Africa's dependence on imported construction materials.
cement.strategicContext: West Africa faces a fundamental construction materials deficit. The region imports over 15 million tonnes of cement annually, paying premium prices that inflate infrastructure costs by 40-70% compared to markets with domestic production. Gambia, with a population of 2.5 million and a GDP growing at 6% annually, currently imports 100% of its cement — a structural vulnerability that increases with every infrastructure project. Harch Cement's 500kT/yr facility captures a significant share of this demand while building domestic industrial capacity that strengthens economic sovereignty.
cement.marketAnalysis: The West African cement market is valued at $8.5 billion and growing at 8% CAGR, driven by urbanization, government infrastructure programs totaling $45 billion across ECOWAS nations, and a housing deficit exceeding 50 million units. Gambia alone imports 400,000 tonnes of cement annually at premium prices averaging $120/tonne versus $65-75/tonne for domestically produced cement.
cement.sustainability: Harch Cement integrates sustainability at every level of operations. Our green cement formulations use locally sourced pozzolanic materials to reduce the clinker factor below 85%, cutting CO2 emissions by 25% versus ordinary Portland cement. The kiln incorporates waste heat recovery technology that captures 30% of thermal energy for power generation, reducing grid electricity consumption. Quarry rehabilitation plans are developed before extraction begins, with progressive restoration using overburden and topsoil stockpiles.

mining.strategicContext: The global energy transition is creating unprecedented demand for critical minerals. Electric vehicle batteries require cobalt and rare earths; solar panels need silicon and tellurium; wind turbines depend on rare earth permanent magnets; and fertilizer production requires phosphate. Africa holds world-class reserves of all these minerals, yet remains primarily a raw material exporter.
mining.marketAnalysis: The global critical minerals market is valued at $320 billion and growing at 12% CAGR. With 1.4 billion people, the world's youngest population, and the largest untapped resource reserves, the continent has the foundations for industrial transformation. Yet it remains structurally dependent on foreign supply chains for its most critical needs — energy, technology, building materials, and food security.

ontology.label: DATA MODEL
ontology.name: Ontology
ontology.description: A unified semantic model that represents every asset, contract, sensor, and operational entity across Harch Corp's eight verticals. The Ontology eliminates data silos and establishes a single source of truth — enabling operators, analysts, and decision-makers to work from the same operational picture, whether they manage a cement plant in Casablanca or a desalination facility in Dakar.

0.title: Unified Object Model
0.description: Every physical asset, legal entity, and operational process modeled as a first-class object with typed properties, provenance, and lineage — from turbines to transport contracts.

1.title: Cross-Vertical Relationship Mapping
1.description: Automatic detection and visualization of dependencies between verticals: how a water shortage impacts cement production, how energy pricing shifts mining output, how logistics bottlenecks cascade across operations.

2.title: Real-Time Data Synchronization
2.description: Bidirectional sync with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle), SCADA networks, IoT sensor arrays, and legacy databases — ensuring the Ontology reflects operational reality, not stale reports.

3.title: Temporal Versioning
3.description: Every object maintains a full history of state changes, enabling retrospective analysis, audit compliance, and point-in-time reconstruction of any operational decision.

foundry.label: DATA INTEGRATION
foundry.name: Foundry
foundry.description: The data integration layer that connects, transforms, and pipelines information from every source Harch Corp operates. Foundry aggregates data from enterprise resource planning systems, legacy databases, SCADA networks, and operational sources to identify bottlenecks, streamline engineering workflows, and support proactive risk mitigation — ultimately providing a unified, data-driven approach to infrastructure management.

0.title: Demand Planning & Procurement Optimization
0.description: Aggregate demand signals across verticals and optimize procurement timelines against supplier capacity, shipping constraints, and storage costs. Reduce overstocking and stockouts through forward-looking pipeline visibility.

1.title: Dynamic Production Scheduling
1.description: Automatically adjust production schedules based on real-time input: equipment availability, energy costs, labor constraints, and downstream demand shifts. Recalibrate in minutes, not days.

2.title: Process Optimization & Non-Compliance Reporting
2.description: Detect process deviations against regulatory and internal thresholds in real time. Generate structured non-compliance reports with root-cause analysis and corrective action recommendations.

3.title: Multi-Source Pipeline Orchestration
3.description: Build, monitor, and audit data pipelines that move information between SAP, Oracle, SQL Server, S3, IoT gateways, and flat files — with full data lineage and quality checks at every stage.

aip.label: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
aip.name: AIP
aip.description: The AI platform layer that enables operators, engineers, and executives to interact with infrastructure data through natural language, build AI-driven workflows, and deploy intelligent automation across operations. AIP goes beyond chat: it builds AI applications, action-driven logic, and production automations that run on operational data — not training datasets.

0.title: AI-Driven Workflow Builder
0.description: Design, test, and deploy AI-powered workflows that combine large language models with operational data. Build automations that monitor conditions, evaluate options, and propose actions for human review — not black-box decisions.

1.title: Action-Driven Logic
1.description: Define business rules and decision logic that trigger real operational actions: reallocate materials, adjust production parameters, escalate maintenance tickets, or reroute logistics — all with full audit trails and human-in-the-loop controls.

2.title: Scenario Simulation & Stress Testing
2.description: Run Monte Carlo simulations and stress tests against real operational constraints: what happens to cement output if energy prices rise 15%? What if the Tangier port shuts for 48 hours? Quantified answers, not guesses.

3.title: Predictive Maintenance & Anomaly Detection
3.description: Pattern recognition across sensor data, maintenance logs, and operational telemetry to identify equipment failures before they occur. Reduce unplanned downtime and extend asset lifespan with evidence-based maintenance scheduling.

apollo.label: DEPLOYMENT & OPERATIONS
apollo.name: Apollo
apollo.description: The deployment and operations engine that manages HarchOS software across production environments — from data centers in Casablanca to edge nodes in remote mining sites. Apollo handles versioning, rollout strategy, health monitoring, and rollback, ensuring that every update to HarchOS reaches every site safely and without downtime.

0.title: Zero-Downtime Continuous Deployment
0.description: Deploy HarchOS updates across all production environments with canary strategies, blue-green rollouts, and automatic health gates. Every deployment is reversible, every change is tracked.

1.title: Multi-Region Operations Management
1.description: Monitor and manage HarchOS instances across Morocco, Senegal, Ivory Coast, and emerging markets from a single control plane. Regional isolation with centralized visibility.

2.title: Automated Rollback & Incident Response
2.description: When a deployment fails health checks, Apollo automatically reverts to the last stable version and generates an incident report with root-cause analysis. Mean time to recovery measured in seconds, not hours.

3.title: Infrastructure Access Control
3.description: Granular, role-based access to production environments with full audit logging. No shared credentials, no untracked SSH sessions, no exceptions.

build.label: INFRASTRUCTURE CONSTRUCTION
build.name: Build
build.description: The construction management platform for Harch Corp's infrastructure pipeline. Build aggregates data from project management systems, site surveys, contractor databases, and financial models to identify schedule risks, optimize resource allocation, and support proactive risk mitigation — providing a unified, data-driven approach to construction project delivery from feasibility to commissioning.

0.title: Demand Planning & Resource Optimization
0.description: Forecast material, labor, and equipment demand across active construction projects. Optimize procurement and allocation against supplier constraints, logistics capacity, and seasonal availability.

1.title: Dynamic Construction Scheduling
1.description: Automatically adjust project schedules based on weather data, contractor availability, supply chain delays, and regulatory approvals. Recalculate critical paths in real time.

2.title: Process Optimization for Compliance Reporting
2.description: Track compliance with environmental permits, safety regulations, and contractual milestones. Generate structured reports for regulators, insurers, and financing partners with source-verified data.

3.title: Site Selection & Terrain Analysis
3.description: Integrate geospatial data, environmental impact assessments, and infrastructure connectivity models to evaluate and compare potential construction sites before committing capital.

intelligence.headerDescription: The operating layer for sovereign AI compute — from GPU scheduling to carbon-aware workload routing across five Moroccan hubs. Every module is built for infrastructure that must never leave African jurisdiction.

0.label: COMPUTE
0.name: Compute Fabric
0.description: Central orchestration layer for GPU clusters across all five hubs. Manages workload placement, queue prioritization, and real-time capacity allocation. Carbon-aware scheduling routes each job to the hub with the lowest grid carbon intensity at that moment — a capability no competitor offers at this granularity.

0.title: Carbon-Aware Scheduling
0.description: Real-time workload routing based on grid carbon intensity per hub. Jobs are automatically placed at the greenest available location, achieving an average portfolio carbon intensity significantly below industry benchmarks. Scheduling decisions factor in 47 parameters including weather forecasts, grid mix, and job urgency.

1.title: Multi-Hub Orchestration
1.description: Unified control plane across five geographically distributed hubs — Ouarzazate, Dakhla, Benguerir, Tanger, and Casablanca. Distributed training jobs can span multiple sites with consistent performance, while failover policies ensure zero-loss job migration during maintenance windows.

2.title: GPU Fleet Management
2.description: Full lifecycle management of heterogeneous GPU inventory — H100, A100, and L40S accelerators. Automated health monitoring, thermal throttling alerts, and predictive replacement scheduling minimize downtime. Capacity planning tools project demand against inventory with quarterly granularity.

3.title: Queue & Priority Management
3.description: Fair-share and priority-based job queuing with SLA enforcement. Reserved capacity guarantees for enterprise customers, burst capacity for spot workloads, and preemption policies that protect production jobs while maximizing cluster utilization.

1.label: SOVEREIGNTY
1.name: Sovereign Data
1.description: Ensures all data processed within Harch Intelligence remains under African jurisdiction. Data residency is enforced at the infrastructure level — not merely as a policy — with encryption, access controls, and audit trails that satisfy Moroccan Law 09-08, AU data frameworks, and international compliance standards.

0.title: Jurisdiction Enforcement
0.description: Infrastructure-level data residency guarantees. All storage, compute, and network traffic remains within Moroccan borders by default. No data traverses foreign jurisdiction unless explicitly authorized by the customer. Physical and logical controls are independently audited quarterly.

1.title: Encryption & Key Management
1.description: End-to-end encryption with customer-managed keys (BYOK). Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256, in transit using TLS 1.3, and during computation using confidential computing enclaves where supported. Key management services operate exclusively within African infrastructure.

2.title: Access & Identity Control
2.description: Role-based access control with multi-factor authentication, session recording, and privileged access management. All access events are logged in an immutable audit trail with 7-year retention. Integration with enterprise SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC.

3.title: Compliance Automation
3.description: Continuous compliance monitoring for GDPR, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and Moroccan Law 09-08. Automated evidence collection, policy-as-code enforcement, and real-time drift detection reduce audit preparation from months to days.

2.label: CONNECTIVITY
2.name: Network Gateway
2.description: Manages the submarine cable infrastructure that connects Morocco to Europe, the Americas, and the Middle East. This is the only African GPU cloud with direct landing of four submarine cable systems — providing the lowest-latency paths between African compute and global data sources.

0.title: Submarine Cable Hub
0.description: Direct integration with four submarine cable systems — ACE, MainOne, Maroc Telecom, and additional capacity via consortium cables. Dual diverse landing stations ensure path redundancy for all international traffic. Total available capacity exceeds 80 Tbps with expansion options.

1.title: Latency Optimization
1.description: Sub-8ms round-trip to European financial centers, sub-35ms to the Americas, and sub-20ms to the Middle East. Anycast routing, traffic engineering, and dedicated wavelengths for latency-sensitive workloads like high-frequency trading and real-time inference.

2.title: Peering & Interconnection
2.description: Carrier-neutral interconnection with direct on-ramps to major cloud providers, internet exchanges, and content delivery networks. Private cross-connects available for enterprise customers requiring dedicated, non-shared bandwidth.

3.title: Network Observability
3.description: Real-time monitoring of all network paths with automated failover detection. Latency heatmap, packet loss tracking, and bandwidth utilization per cable system. Alerts for degradation events with root cause analysis tools.

3.label: OBSERVABILITY
3.name: Platform Monitor
3.description: Full-stack observability across all five hubs — from GPU die temperature to PUE to carbon intensity per job. Integrates with customer Grafana instances and provides managed dashboards for teams that need visibility without infrastructure overhead.

0.title: GPU & Infrastructure Metrics
0.description: Real-time telemetry for GPU utilization, VRAM consumption, thermal throttling events, and power draw per accelerator. Infrastructure-level metrics include PUE, cooling efficiency, power distribution, and network throughput per hub.

1.title: Carbon Intensity Tracking
1.description: Per-job carbon accounting that measures the actual grid carbon intensity at the hub where each workload ran. Cumulative carbon reports per project, per team, or per organization enable accurate sustainability reporting without estimation.

2.title: Cost & Billing Analytics
2.description: Transparent cost breakdowns by GPU type, utilization tier, and job duration. Reserved instance savings calculators, spot pricing history, and budget alerts. Exportable billing data in standard formats for integration with procurement systems.

3.title: Alerting & Incident Response
3.description: Configurable alert policies with multi-channel notification — email, webhook, PagerDuty integration. Automated incident timelines, correlated log aggregation, and suggested remediation paths reduce mean time to resolution.

cement.headerDescription: The digital backbone of vertically integrated cement production — from quarry bench planning to finished product delivery. Each module covers a distinct phase of the value chain, ensuring full traceability from limestone face to construction site.

0.label: EXTRACTION
0.name: Quarry & Raw Materials
0.description: Manages the full quarry lifecycle from geological survey through bench extraction to raw material quality control. With over 50 years of verified limestone reserves, this module ensures consistent feedstock supply while minimizing extraction waste and environmental impact.

0.title: Reserve Mapping & Planning
0.description: 3D geological models of limestone reserves with chemical composition mapping by bench and layer. Extraction planning tools optimize bench sequencing for consistent raw material quality while minimizing overburden removal. Quarterly reserve updates based on drilling program results.

1.title: Blast Design & Execution
1.description: Precision blast design software that calculates charge patterns, timing sequences, and fragmentation targets. Post-blast analysis via drone survey compares actual fragmentation against design, enabling continuous refinement. Vibration monitoring ensures compliance with local environmental standards.

2.title: Raw Material Quality Control
2.description: Automated sampling and XRF analysis at the crusher feed with real-time chemical composition dashboards. If limestone chemistry deviates from target ranges, the system recommends blending ratios from alternative quarry faces to maintain consistent kiln feed quality.

3.title: Environmental Compliance
3.description: Dust monitoring stations around the quarry perimeter with real-time PM10/PM25 tracking. Blasting schedule optimization to minimize community impact. Progressive rehabilitation plans triggered automatically as benches are depleted, using stockpiled topsoil and overburden.

1.label: PRODUCTION
1.name: Kiln Operations
1.description: Controls the heart of the cement plant — from raw meal preparation through clinker production to finish grinding. The 5-stage preheater with calciner achieves energy consumption significantly below regional averages, while AI-optimized kiln control reduces fuel waste and improves clinker quality.

0.title: Kiln Process Control
0.description: AI-driven kiln control system that manages flame temperature, rotational speed, feed rate, and airflow in real time. Predictive models trained on historical production data anticipate coating buildup and ring formation, enabling preventive adjustments that reduce unplanned shutdowns.

1.title: Waste Heat Recovery
1.description: Captures approximately 30% of exhaust heat from the preheater and clinker cooler for power generation. The recovered energy feeds back into plant operations, reducing grid electricity consumption. Performance monitoring tracks heat recovery efficiency and identifies degradation in heat exchanger performance.

2.title: Alternative Fuel Management
2.description: Tracking and optimization of alternative fuel substitution rates — including agricultural waste, tire-derived fuel, and municipal solid waste fractions. The system balances substitution rate against clinker quality requirements and emissions limits, maximizing cost savings without compromising product standards.

3.title: Quality Assurance
3.description: ISO 9001-certified quality management with automated sampling at every production stage — raw meal, clinker, and finished cement. Real-time free lime monitoring, Blaine fineness tracking, and compressive strength prediction models ensure product consistency that exceeds EN 197 and ASTM C150 standards.

2.label: FORMULATION
2.name: Green Formulations
2.description: Develops and manages lower-carbon cement products that reduce the clinker factor without sacrificing performance. Current formulations use locally sourced pozzolanic materials, while the R&D pipeline targets LC3 (calcined clay) formulations for further carbon reduction by 2029.

0.title: Clinker Factor Optimization
0.description: Systematic reduction of the clinker-to-cement ratio through supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). Current blended cement formulations achieve a clinker factor below 85%, with a clear roadmap to sub-70% using LC3 technology. Each formulation is validated against strength, durability, and setting time requirements.

1.title: LC3 Development Pipeline
1.description: Active R&D program for Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3), which can reduce carbon emissions by up to 40% compared to ordinary Portland cement. Lab-scale validation is complete, with pilot production planned for 2028 and commercial launch targeted for 2029. Raw material sourcing from local clay deposits has been confirmed.

2.title: Carbon Tracking per Product
2.description: Life-cycle carbon accounting for each cement product, from quarry extraction through production to factory gate. Product-specific carbon intensity data enables customers to report embodied carbon in their construction projects accurately — a requirement under emerging EU CBAM regulations.

3.title: Certification & Standards
3.description: All green formulations undergo certification against relevant standards — EN 197 for cement, EN 206 for concrete, and LEED/BREEAM credit compliance documentation. The system maintains current certification status, expiry dates, and renewal workflows for each product-market combination.

3.label: LOGISTICS
3.name: Distribution & Delivery
3.description: Coordinates the physical supply chain from plant gate to customer site — managing river barge scheduling, road tanker dispatch, and customer order fulfillment across a 500km distribution radius covering Gambia, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea.

0.title: Order Management
0.description: Customer order intake via phone, WhatsApp, and web portal with automated order confirmation and delivery scheduling. Priority allocation during high-demand periods, volume-based pricing tiers, and contract management for long-term offtake agreements.

1.title: Fleet Dispatch & Tracking
1.description: Real-time dispatch management for a fleet of cement tankers and river barges. GPS tracking of all vehicles, ETAs updated dynamically based on traffic and road conditions, and proof-of-delivery capture via driver mobile app. Fleet utilization analytics identify underperforming routes.

2.title: River Transport Coordination
2.description: Barge loading and scheduling on the Gambia River — the lowest-cost bulk transport method for interior markets. Tidal window planning, barge capacity optimization, and multi-stop routing for customers along the river corridor. Direct barge access provides cost advantages that road-only competitors cannot match.

3.title: Inventory & Demand Forecasting
3.description: Warehouse and silo inventory tracking with automated reorder points. Demand forecasting models incorporate construction seasonality, government project pipelines, and historical sales patterns. Alerts for stockout risk and overproduction ensure optimal inventory levels.

energy.headerDescription: End-to-end management of renewable energy generation, grid integration, and storage — from individual inverter monitoring to portfolio-level dispatch optimization. Designed for Morocco's exceptional solar irradiance and Atlantic wind resources.

overview.label: Overview
overview.title: Capturing the value chain
overview.body: Africa holds 30% of the world's mineral reserves but captures only 5% of the value. Harch Mining changes this. We extract, process, and sell strategic minerals in-country — phosphate for fertilizer, cobalt for batteries, rare earths for EVs. Every kilogram processed in Morocco or Gambia stays in Africa, creating jobs and sovereignty.

hardware.label: Hardware
hardware.title: Vertically integrated extraction
hardware.body: From geological survey to processed concentrate, every step under our control. Open-pit and underground operations. Heavy equipment fleet (Caterpillar, Komatsu). On-site processing plants with flotation, magnetic separation, hydrometallurgy. Real-time ore grade monitoring via XRF. Tailings management per GISTM standards.

reliability.label: Reliability
reliability.title: Sustainable mining, certified
reliability.body: Every Harch Mining site operates under IRMA (Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance) standards. Independent annual audits. Water recycling rate: 85%. products.d: 3D geological modeling with AI-predicted ore grades. Blast patterns optimized for grade recovery. 15% reduction in waste rock.

Satellite + IoT sensor monitoring of tailings dams. Alert system per GISTM standard. Independent third-party audit data integrated.

tailings.label: Tailings
tailings.title: Tailings dams built to the GISTM standard
tailings.body: Tailings are the single largest risk in mining. We treat them as such. Every Harch tailings storage facility is designed, built, and operated to the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM). Independent third-party engineers audit the dam annually. Satellite InSAR monitors wall movement to the millimetre. A rehabilitation bond is posted before first tailings are placed — the land is paid for before it is touched.

irmaCert.label: IRMA
irmaCert.title: Independently audited against the IRMA standard
irmaCert.body: The Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) is the only multi-stakeholder audit built by NGOs, communities, and miners together. We audit every producing site against it — publicly, with the full scorecard published. No other standard comes close on transparency.

items.d: Water recycling 85%. Land rehabilitation bond. Biodiversity offset ratio 2:1. Zero discharge to rivers from process water.
Community development agreement signed before extraction. Free, prior, informed consent process. Local hiring quota 70%. Grievance mechanism within 48h.
Anti-corruption audit. Beneficial ownership disclosed. Tax payments published country-by-country. No offshoring.
IRMA results are not pass/fail — they are a public scorecard 0–100 per criteria. Ours are published on the IRMA website.

inCountry.label: In-country
inCountry.title: 100% of ore processed on African soil
inCountry.body: For 150 years, Africa's mineral wealth left as raw ore — and 95% of the value left with it. We end that. Every tonne we mine is processed to a saleable concentrate in-country. No raw ore export, ever. The jobs stay. The tax base stays. The downstream industries — battery precursors, fertilizer, magnet alloys — become possible.

offtakePartners.label: Offtake
offtakePartners.title: Pre-sold to the world's largest industrial buyers

No spot market exposure.

mineralsTransition.label: Energy transition
mineralsTransition.title: The minerals beneath the energy transition
mineralsTransition.body: Every wind turbine, every EV, every battery cell, every fertilizer granule begins as rock in the ground. The energy transition is, fundamentally, a mineral transition — and the minerals have to come from somewhere responsible. From us.

items.d: P2O5 concentrate to OCP and IFFCO. Phosphate is the bottleneck of global food production — half the world's food depends on phosphate fertilizer. Morocco holds 70% of global reserves. We extract and process it responsibly.

Cobalt sulfate for NMC and NCA lithium-ion cathodes. Sold to CATL, LG Energy, Tesla. RMI traceable, IRMA audited. The Bou Azzer mine has produced cobalt since 1928 — we are its modern, responsible operator.

Neodymium and praseodymium for permanent magnets in EV motors and wind turbines. 92% of global supply currently comes from China. Our Baldou pilot is one of very few ex-China sources on the African continent.

extraction.label: Extraction
extraction.title: Open-pit and underground, ore-grade in real time
extraction.body: Every truck that leaves the pit is scanned by an XRF analyzer mounted on the haul road. The ore grade is known before the truck reaches the primary crusher. Low-grade material is diverted to stockpile; high-grade goes straight to the mill. The result: 15% less waste rock hauled, 3% higher mill recovery, and zero mis-classified loads.

solarProcess.label: Solar Process
solarProcess.title: From feasibility to commissioning in six months
solarProcess.body: Every Harch Energy solar project follows a single, audited workflow — engineered to deliver Tier-1 generation assets on schedule and under budget. Our project directors map every milestone from the first site survey to the final performance test, with 30/30/30/10 milestone payments that protect your cash flow at every phase.

steps.d: Site survey, irradiance modelling, ONEE interconnection study, and a full lifecycle savings report delivered within 14 days. We benchmark your current bill against three system sizes and lock in the savings envelope before you commit.

Single-line diagrams, structural calculations, fire code compliance, and ONEE convention d'accueil. Harch Energy handles every permit — municipal, electrical, environmental — so nothing stalls in administration.

Tier-1 Jinko Solar or LONGi modules, Huawei or Sungrow inverters, and Mounting Systems structures shipped from our Casablanca warehouse. FDE subsidy paperwork filed in parallel to recover up to 30% of CAPEX.

In-house crews install the mounting structure, modules, inverters, and AC/DC cabling. Daily safety briefings, weekly progress photos, and live KPIs in your client portal — no black-box subcontracting.

Performance ratio test against IEC 61724, grid synchronization with ONEE, dashboard activation, and operator training. You sign acceptance only when the plant hits nameplate output for three consecutive days.
24/7 remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, annual preventive visit, and a 48-hour on-site intervention SLA. The Harch Energy O&M contract runs for the full 25-year panel warranty period.

windPower.label: Wind Power
windPower.title: Onshore wind at industrial scale
windPower.body: Harch Energy designs, builds and operates onshore wind farms from 5 MW captive installations to 200 MW merchant plants. Our turbines are sourced from Goldwind, Envision and Vestas — three of the top five global OEMs — and certified for Morocco's high-temperature, high-salt environments. Every farm ships with a 20-year full-service contract and a 95% availability guarantee written into the PPA.

hydrogen.label: Green Hydrogen
hydrogen.title: Green hydrogen for Morocco's industrial decarbonization
hydrogen.body: Harch Energy is building Morocco's first vertically integrated green hydrogen valley near Dakhla. Powered by 1.8 GW of dedicated solar and wind, the plant will produce 200,000 tonnes of green ammonia per year for export to Europe and for domestic fertilizer production. Electrolysis is handled by 1.2 GW of alkaline and PEM stacks from our technology partners, with brine and water management co-located with the Harch Water desalination plant.

steps.d: Co-located solar PV and onshore wind feed the electrolyzers directly, with a 4-hour battery buffer smoothing intermittency. No grid draw — every electron is green by origin.
Seawater from the Harch Water desalination plant is polished to <0.1 µS/cm conductivity before electrolysis. Zero freshwater consumption — the entire facility runs on the Atlantic.
Alkaline stacks (1.0 GW) handle base-load hydrogen production; PEM stacks (0.2 GW) follow solar peaks. Total output: 90,000 Nm³/h of 99.998% pure hydrogen.
Hydrogen reacts with nitrogen from an air separation unit to produce green ammonia at 180 bar. Output: 200,000 t/year of NH₃, shipped from the adjacent Tiznit port terminal.

video.title: Powering Morocco, one electron at a time
video.body: From the Sahara sun to the Atlantic wind, our crews design, build and operate the energy infrastructure that powers Moroccan industry. Press play for a 60-second tour of our solar, wind and hydrogen assets.

software.label: Software
software.title: Real-time optimization, in your pocket
software.body: The Harch Energy platform is the brain behind every plant we operate. It ingests 4 million data points per day from your inverters, meters, batteries and weather stations — then runs a predictive model that decides when to store, when to consume, and when to sell surplus back to the ONEE grid. Every customer gets a free mobile app and a 24/7 remote operations team backing it.

products.d: Real-time production, consumption and savings dashboard accessible from any phone, tablet or laptop. Role-based access for plant managers, CFOs and maintenance crews.
A reinforcement-learning model trained on 18 months of your site data decides hourly whether to store, self-consume or export — adding 7-12% to your annual savings with no human intervention.

Vibration, temperature and current signatures from every inverter and tracker are compared to a fleet-wide baseline. Failures are flagged 14-30 days before they happen — annual preventive visit included.

aiNetwork.label: Smart Grid
aiNetwork.title: A self-healing grid for the renewable era
aiNetwork.body: As solar and wind penetration rises, the Moroccan grid needs software that can react in milliseconds — not minutes. Harch Energy's smart-grid platform orchestrates storage, demand response and curtailment across every site we operate, providing ancillary services to ONEE and keeping your plant compliant with the latest grid codes.

items.d: Battery inverters respond to frequency events in under 200 ms, earning primary reserve payments from ONEE while protecting your plant from trips.
Non-critical loads (chillers, compressors, EV chargers) are throttled automatically during peak tariff windows — a 4-9% reduction in demand charges with zero comfort impact.
A neural network trained on 12 years of Météo-Maroc data predicts your solar output 72 hours ahead with a 4.1% nMAE — tight enough to bid into the day-ahead market.
When the grid is congested, our optimizer routes surplus into batteries, electrolyzers or controllable loads before ONEE curtails your production. Recovered revenue: 2-3% of annual generation.

storage.label: Storage
storage.title: Lithium-ion batteries, engineered for the Moroccan climate
storage.body: Every Harch Energy solar farm can be paired with a lithium-ion battery system sized from 4 hours to 8 hours of autonomy. Cells are LFP chemistry from CATL or BYD — the safest, longest-cycle-life chemistry on the market — housed in IP54 containers with active liquid cooling. The system is warranted for 6,000 cycles or 10 years, whichever comes first, with a guaranteed end-of-warranty capacity of 80%.

whyHarch.body: Harch Energy is the only Moroccan player that owns the entire stack: Tier-1 hardware, software, EPC crews, O&M network and project finance. Harch Corp is one of Morocco's most ambitious planned industrial groups. Every contract is designed to be backed by the parent balance sheet — not a project-finance special purpose vehicle.
Twelve regional service centers planned across Morocco, to be staffed 24/7, with a contractual 48-hour on-site response time. We never outsource after-sales.
We file your FDE energy-efficiency subsidy, your tax exemption dossier, and your ONEE self-consumption convention — recovering 25-30% of CAPEX before commissioning.

items.q: How long does it take to install a Harch Energy solar farm?
items.a: A typical 1-5 MW rooftop or ground-mount installation takes 6-8 months from signed contract to commissioning. That breaks down into 14 days of feasibility, 45 days of engineering and permitting, 60 days of procurement, 90 days of construction, and 15 days of commissioning and performance testing. Larger utility-scale plants and wind farms scale linearly with capacity.

items.q: Do I need to buy the system, or can Harch own it?
items.a: You have four options: (1) Buy the system outright with milestone billing 30/30/30/10. (2) Lease it from Harch Energy over 10 years. (3) Sign a Power Purchase Agreement where Harch owns the plant and sells you electricity per kWh. (4) Sign a 25-year Build-Operate-Transfer where Harch owns the plant and transfers it to you at zero cost at the end. All four structures use the same Tier-1 hardware and the same O&M SLA.

items.q: What happens during a grid outage?
items.a: If your system includes battery storage (4-8 hours of autonomy), the system automatically islands itself and continues powering your critical loads. The transfer takes under 200 milliseconds — fast enough that most industrial PLCs and IT systems do not notice. If you do not have batteries, the solar inverters shut down per ONEE anti-islanding requirements, and your plant re-syncs when the grid returns.

Tier-1 panel manufacturers (Jinko Solar, LONGi) warrant the modules for 25 years at 80% of nameplate output. Harch Energy extends that warranty by adding a 10-year installation warranty covering inverters, mounting structure, cabling and workmanship. From year 10 to year 25, the O&M contract covers preventive maintenance, remote monitoring, and any inverter replacement needed. Battery systems come with a separate 10-year / 6,000-cycle warranty.

items.q: Can I sell my surplus electricity back to ONEE?
items.a: Yes — under Morocco's Loi 13-09 self-consumption framework, you can sign a convention d'autoconsommation with ONEE that lets you inject surplus production into the grid. Harch Energy handles the entire administrative process. The buy-back tariff is currently set at the medium-voltage tariff minus a wheeling charge; the AI optimizer in our platform automatically dispatches surplus to the grid when it is financially advantageous.

items.q: What subsidies and tax incentives are available?
items.a: The Fonds de Développement Énergétique (FDE) covers up to 30% of CAPEX for energy-efficiency projects above 1 million MAD. Renewable energy equipment is also exempt from VAT and from customs duties. Harch Energy files the FDE subsidy, the VAT exemption, and the customs paperwork as part of the EPC contract — we recover the funds before commissioning and pass them through to you.

It's a model trained on 50,000+ real African farm-seasons — soil types from Senegal's laterites to Mali's alluvials, weather patterns from Sahelian droughts to Guinean monsoons, crop responses across 12 staple species. Every morning, it ingests your sensor data, satellite NDVI, and 7-day forecast, then pushes a single recommendation to your phone: irrigate 12 mm today, scout the north field for fall armyworm, harvest the eastern block on Friday.

We embed agronomists in every cooperative we serve — not call-center agents, not WhatsApp bots, but trained agronomists who walk your fields, know your soil, and remember last season's drought. They translate the AI's recommendations into action. They catch what sensors miss. They are why our cooperatives renew at 94%.

markets.title: Direct from farmgate to buyer, no middlemen
markets.body: A Senegalese farmer grows a kilo of millet for 280 CFA. A middleman buys it for 320. A processor pays 540. The farmer captured 12% of the final price. Harch Markets changes the math. Our digital marketplace connects cooperatives directly to processors, exporters, and retailers. Bids are transparent. Payment is escrowed. Logistics are coordinated. The farmer captures 60-70% of the final price.

financing.label: Financing
financing.title: 0% for cooperatives. Lease-to-own for estates.

In Morocco, we handle Tamwilcom guarantee paperwork end-to-end for qualifying cooperatives at 0% interest. In Senegal, we work with BNDE and FAARF. In Côte d'Ivoire, OSNEA. Repayment is tied to harvest revenue, so the technology pays for itself. For commercial estates, we offer 3-year lease-to-own. No farm is too small to modernize.

5,000 m³ treated-water reservoirs. UV disinfection. Continuous turbidity monitoring.
Pressurized network with smart meters. AI demand forecasting. 23% loss reduction vs legacy networks.

items.d: LSTM models forecast demand 72 hours ahead, 94% accuracy. Plant output adjusts automatically. No more over-production at night.

items.q: What is desalination and how does it work?
items.a: Desalination removes salt from seawater to produce drinking water. We use reverse osmosis: high-pressure pumps force seawater through membranes that block 99.7% of salt. Energy recovery turbines capture 96% of the pressure energy, bringing total consumption to 3.5 kWh/m³ — 30% below industry average.

items.q: Is desalinated water safe to drink?
items.a: Yes. Our water meets WHO drinking water standards. Continuous online monitoring of turbidity, pH, free chlorine, and TDS. Every batch gets a QR-coded certificate of analysis. Remineralization restores calcium and magnesium to natural levels.

items.q: How does the AI network reduce losses?
items.a: 1,247 smart sensors monitor pressure, flow, and quality at every network node. AI detects leaks in <60 seconds, localizes them within 50 meters, and dispatches crews before customers notice. Reinforcement learning optimizes pressure zone-by-zone, cutting energy use 18% and pipe bursts 31%.

items.q: What are the BOT and BOO models?
items.a: Build-Operate-Transfer: we invest the capex, build the plant, operate it for 15-25 years, then transfer it to you. Build-Own-Operate: same, but we retain ownership. In both cases you pay only for water delivered, with no capital outlay.

items.q: How long does it take to build a desalination plant?
items.a: Fixed-price EPC in 24 months from contract signature. Permit & EIA: 3 months. Design: 3 months. Construction: 18 months. Commissioning: 2 months. Long-lead items (membranes, high-pressure pumps) ordered in Month 1.

items.q: What happens if uptime drops below 99.5%?
items.a: Service-level agreement includes automatic credits. If a network fails completely, our emergency response mobilizes within 48 hours — mobile 500 m³/day desalination unit, tanker fleet, and bottled water reserves pre-positioned with the Moroccan Red Crescent.

items.q: Can you serve remote or off-grid communities?
items.a: Yes. Our solar desalination pilots (Tan-Tan 2026) need no grid connection. Atmospheric water generators harvest 5,000 L/day from humid air for villages without any water source. Both solutions are designed for off-grid deployment.

100% renewable-powered (solar + wind + hydro storage). 3.5 kWh/m³ — 30% below industry. Brine mining pilot (2027) extracts lithium and magnesium from RO brine instead of discharging it. We achieve -42,000 tons CO₂ avoided per year per plant.

solution.label: THE SOLUTION
solution.title: We optimize your presence for AI engines. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, GLM.
solution.body: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the discipline of making AI models cite your business. We audit what AIs say about you today, fix the gaps in their knowledge, create content that AIs love to cite, build your entity on Wikidata and Wikipedia, and monitor your visibility monthly across every major AI engine. This is not SEO. This is GEO.

items.d: We run 200+ queries against ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and GLM. We map exactly what each AI knows — and does not know — about your business.
We create the content, structured data, and entity records that fill the gaps in the AI's training. Wikidata, Wikipedia, authoritative citations, schema.org markup.
AI engines re-train and re-rank continuously. We run the same 200 queries every month, measure your visibility, ship updates, and send you a board-ready report.

items.a: SEO optimizes for Google blue links. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) optimizes for AI engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, GLM. SEO gets you to rank #3 on a Google page. GEO gets the AI to name you in its answer. Different engines, different signals, different work. Most businesses need both — but GEO is where the next 5 years of demand is going.

items.q: Will ChatGPT change its algorithm and undo all the work?
items.a: AI engines re-train continuously, so visibility drifts — that is exactly why the monthly monitoring retainer exists. But the foundation we build (Wikidata entity, Wikipedia page, schema.org structured data, authoritative citations) is permanent. It is part of the AI's training corpus. Even if ChatGPT re-ranks, your entity is now in its memory. Cancellation does not erase you.

items.q: How long until I appear in ChatGPT?
items.a: Typical timeline: 4-8 weeks from setup start to first citation in ChatGPT. Perplexity is faster (2-4 weeks — it crawls more aggressively). Google AI Overviews is slower (8-16 weeks — it depends on Google's index refresh). GLM is fastest for francophone content (2-3 weeks). The free audit sets realistic per-engine timelines for your specific category.

Because the audit sells the setup. We run 200+ queries across 4 AI engines, show you exactly what each AI says about you, name the competitors it cites instead, and quantify the revenue you are losing. After seeing that, ~70% of audited businesses buy the setup. The other 30% take the report and do the work themselves. Both outcomes are fine — the audit is genuinely free, no email gate, no commitment.

items.q: Can you guarantee I will appear in ChatGPT?
items.a: No reputable GEO agency can guarantee a specific citation. AI engines are black boxes — we cannot force ChatGPT to cite you. What we can guarantee: we will build the entity, content, structured data, and citations that make you cite-able. We will measure your visibility monthly. We will iterate until you appear. If after 6 months you are still invisible, we keep working for free until you do.

items.q: What about data sovereignty and Loi 09-08?
items.a: We use GLM-4 by Z.ai — no US provider, no US export control, no Patriot Act exposure. Your audit data, your entity records, your content — all processed in a jurisdiction compatible with Loi 09-08. For ultra-sensitive clients, GLM-4 weights are downloadable and we can run inference on infrastructure you control. We provide a Loi 09-08 cheat sheet (free, no email gate) detailing what is legal to process where.

Three tiers. Audit: 0 MAD, 1 week, free. Setup: 30-80K MAD depending on category competitiveness and existing digital footprint, 2-4 weeks, fixed scope agreed at the end of the audit. Retainer: 5-15K MAD/month, cancel anytime with 30-day notice. Payment by bank transfer (RIB) — Moroccan RIB, French IBAN, or international wire. No Stripe, no card fees. Setup: 50% upfront, 50% on delivery.

items.q: We have an SEO agency. Do we fire them?
items.a: Probably not. SEO and GEO are complementary, not competing. Your SEO agency optimizes for Google blue links (still valuable — Google AI Overviews pulls from Google's index). We optimize for ChatGPT, Perplexity, and GLM (which pull from their own training data and live web crawls). Many clients keep their SEO agency for Google and add us for AI engines. The free audit will tell you whether your SEO agency is already covering AI — most are not.
